Our observationally equivalent constructions establish unavoidable timing regret at any sample size for a fixed observation length, while exact certificates determine whether all compatible populations share a unique optimal date. Matched experiments separate the effects of estimation, bootstrap averaging, and regret weighting. Longer observation often resolves timing ambiguity, but the optimal date may already have passed. In our experiments, bootstrap averaging and early stopping improve decisions, while regret weighting adds no improvement in pooled mean squared regret: better statistical fit need not yield better allocation welfare. The code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/waiting-buys-two-moments.
n1296bbed0bc8: We present GINNGER (GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for GEnerative Rheology), a framework for discovering thermodynamically admissible constitutive equations from microstructural flow data. Unlike existing approaches that learn constitutive operators, GINNGER reformulates constitutive discovery as the learning of the underlying thermodynamic generators from which constitutive equations emerge. Embedding the GENERIC formalism into the learning process restricts the search to constitutive models that satisfy the first and second laws of thermodynamics by construction, eliminating the need to prescribe phenomenological constitutive equations a priori. A second conceptual advance is a spectral formulation of constitutive discovery in the intrinsic eigenspace of the polymer conformation tensor. This provides a kinematics-independent thermodynamic state space in which the thermodynamic generators depend only on the instantaneous microstructural state, while flow kinematics acts solely as an external driver transporting the system through this space. Consequently, data from shear, extensional, and mixed flows contribute to the discovery of a single constitutive model that generalizes across deformation protocols and flow geometries. By learning thermodynamic generators rather than high-dimensional constitutive operators, GINNGER substantially reduces the complexity of the discovery problem while preserving thermodynamic consistency, material objectivity, and physical interpretability by construction. The framework is validated using high-fidelity simulations, accurately reconstructing constitutive behavior and predicting complex flow fields across previously unseen geometries. GINNGER establishes a new paradigm for constitutive discovery by combining generative, spectral, and thermodynamically grounded learning within a unified framework for data-driven modeling of complex fluids.
n7f16b353b327: Collective synchronization is a common response of interacting magnetic particles subjected to rotating external fields. Here we demonstrate a distinct nonequilibrium state in a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles in which the ordered crystalline core rotates, on average, opposite to the direction of the applied rotating magnetic field, while the defect-rich outer region continues to rotate with the drive. We term this state anti-synchronized collective rotation. By combining structural, spectral, bond-resolved, and layer-resolved torque analyses, we show that anti-synchronization is associated with a broader defect-rich interface, enhanced and dynamically heterogeneous bond deformation, and a reorganization of torque transmission between the surface and the crystalline interior. In the synchronized state, steric torques compensate the opposing dipolar contribution in the outer core, maintaining a positive net interaction torque. In the anti-synchronized state this compensation becomes insufficient, producing a negative net torque in theouter core and enabling core-surface rotational decoupling. Increasing the driving frequency restores coherent rotation through a transition characterized by competing positive- and negative-angular-velocity populations and hysteresis, consistent with a discontinuous, first-order-like dynamical transition. These results demonstrate how deformation and spatial redistribution of interaction torques can generate counter-rotating collective states in driven colloidal matter.
nf45f8ebf9712: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N=4$ anyons, obtain accurate results up to $N = 16$ for intermediate statistics, and study up to $N=20$ for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.
n043d6f9b9d98: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. The main technical hurdle is then to establish the existence of such a frame whose corresponding lines preserve no symmetry. This can be achieved using the Steiner frame construction of Fickus, Mixon, and Tremain.
n822928502233: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.
nd0c8d2062989: The coexistence of a Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like short range interaction in a single-phase homogeneous manganite is of particular interest because it reveals multiple levels of magnetic clustering generated by disorder and competing exchange interactions. In bulk $\mathrm{La}_{0.19}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.81}\mathrm{MnO}_{3}$, this unusual magnetic state develops in the antiferromagnetic regime, where A-site disorder strongly modifies the local magnetic landscape. Rietveld analysis confirms a single-phase orthorhombic structure, while magnetic measurements establish a Griffiths phase below $T_{\mathrm{G}} = 280\text{ K}$ through the deviation from Curie-Weiss behavior. Superparamagnetic-like behavior persisting from 280 to 370 K further indicates that isolated magnetic clusters remain stable well into the nominally paramagnetic region. The presence of both phenomena highlights the crucial role of disorder-induced exchange randomness in stabilizing complex magnetic states in correlated perovskite oxides.
nb985e448d720: With growing interest in environmental conservation, polymer composites incorporating wood-derived materials have attracted significant attention. While research has focused extensively on hard composites utilizing delignified wood or cellulose nanofibers (CNF) and soft composites reinforced with CNF, there have been a limited number of studies on the development of soft composites that utilize the porous cellular structure of wood, with few exceptions. In this study, we fabricated soft composites by infiltrating delignified wood with polyacrylamide hydrogel and subjected them to uniaxial compression tests. The results demonstrated that these materials exhibited far superior strength and toughness compared to either delignified wood or polyacrylamide hydrogel alone. Through systematic investigation and theoretical analysis, we identified the mechanisms underlying these enhancements in strength and toughness. Specifically, in addition to the sacrificial bond breakage known to enhance toughness in double-network hydrogels, we propose that mechanical confinement, arising from the soft, incompressible hydrogel filling the hollow cell lumens, generates excess stress and acts to resist compressive deformation. This approach, which utilizes the cellular structure as a filler, suggests the potential for creating a new class of high-toughness composite materials.
n072816fc9ce1: Crystal-field (CF) excitations and their coupling to lattice vibrations were investigated in ErFeO$_3$ using inelastic neutron scattering. Pronounced modifications of the excitation spectra, including energy shifts, intensity redistribution, and linewidth changes, were observed as a consequence of CF-phonon coupling. Significant renormalization of the first and second CF excitations, located near 5 meV and 12 meV, respectively, was detected along both transverse and longitudinal directions in the vicinity of the reciprocal-space point Q = (2, 0, 4). The coupling effects become more prominent as the temperature increases from 300 K to 650 K, while a slight suppression is observed at 750 K. Remarkably, CF excitation peaks that are strongly weakened by thermal population effects re-emerge in specific momentum regions through interaction with phonon modes. The coupled excitations exhibit characteristic signatures of hybridization, including energy renormalization, intensity enhancement, and linewidth narrowing. Density-functional-theory-based phonon calculations further support the interpretation of CF-phonon coupling in ErFeO3. These results demonstrate that strong interactions between CF excitations and lattice vibrations can substantially modify the excitation spectra in rare-earth orthoferrites.
n8f7130feb6c7: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
n0e8a50b6d775: Electrochemical processes at charged interfaces lie at the heart of modern technologies and their continued improvement depends on insights into the relevant atomistic processes. However, the necessary tools to impose constant-voltage conditions in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations typically directly target the electrode charge, making their extension to methods that go beyond an empirical description of metals more cumbersome. In this work, we propose an MD protocol to realize a thermodynamic ensemble in which voltage control is attained, but which is formulated purely within the framework of finite-field simulations in 3D periodic boundary conditions. We show a derivation and implementation of such a control device, which we coin an electrostat, in the ELECTRODE package within LAMMPS. Our simulations systematically benchmark the derived theory against other established approaches, for example, showing its equivalence to a potentiostat, and quantify the importance of properly accounting for ensemble fluctuations. We find that for systems of several thousands of atoms, one obtains the same equilibrium properties with the electrostat as with a simpler constant-field simulation. The difference between the two methods only manifests itself at smaller length scales, thereby establishing practical limits for the inclusion of voltage fluctuations in atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems. The strength of this framework also lies in its simplicity of extension to first-principles ab initio and reactive machine-learning potentials.
n4a7d8b4f6fe3: We compute exactly the covariance between the maximum $M$ and the number of records $K$ in a discrete time series of $n$ entries as a quantitative probe of the history leading to an extreme event. For continuous IID series, with a common probability distribution function (PDF) $p(x)$, we find the striking result that $M$ and $K$ are uncorrelated for any $n \geq 1$. We show that this independence is rather fragile and the covariance $C_q(n)$ between $M$ and $K$ becomes nonzero when $p(x)$ becomes discontinuous due to a delta-component at $x=0$ with an amplitude $0q_c$). We compute the critical strength $q_c$ exactly. Furthermore, for large $n$, we show that $C_q(n)$ decays as a power law, with an exponent that depends on the tail of $p(x)$. We then compare our theoretical predictions with real precipitation data from several weather stations across Germany, finding a very good agreement.
nc32afceb1b27: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. Crucially, the induced nonrelativistic and relativistic spin splittings exhibit qualitatively different dependences on band alignment. Virtual processes involving the valence and conduction bands of the altermagnet can reinforce the altermagnetic splitting while contributing with opposite signs to the interfacial Rashba coupling. Consequently, electrostatic tuning can access a regime in which the Rashba splitting vanishes while a sizable $d$-wave spin splitting persists. Exact diagonalization of the full heterostructure model confirms the analytical theory and establishes the robustness of this mechanism beyond the perturbative regime. Our results identify altermagnetic proximity as a route for engineering nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states in established semiconductor platforms, providing a general strategy for disentangling magnetic and relativistic spin interactions in quantum heterostructures.
n71905f0b48f7: The realization of Fulde-Ferrell (FF) superconducting states has long been pursued but remains challenging because of the large Zeeman splitting required. Here, we demonstrate that $p$-wave magnets can host equal-spin finite-pair-momentum states with $p$-wave symmetry, termed FF states, at arbitrarily weak fields. Our Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis shows that, owing to the displacement of the Fermi surface, two equal-spin electrons in the FF states pair at the same energy, just as in the opposite-spin zero-pair-momentum states of the same gap symmetry. At zero field, the FF states are therefore exactly degenerate with these zero-pair-momentum counterparts. An arbitrarily weak Zeeman field lifts this degeneracy and makes the FF states the superconducting ground state, since they remain stable owing to their equal-spin nature, whereas their counterparts are suppressed by the formation of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. These findings identify the fermiology of $p$-wave magnets as a promising route toward long-sought finite-momentum superconductivity.
n1b8f537c7e7b: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.
na15aab4375e7: We study field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions (ICTs) in classical spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) $D$, strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy $A$ within the easy plane. This model describes systems with ferromagnetic layers coupled by exchange interaction with DMI. The magnetic field $\bf H$ is applied in the easy plane at an arbitrary angle $δ$ to the easy axis stabilizing a soliton lattice in the ground state. We consider ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic in-chain exchange interactions within the continuum limit and show that the easy-axis anisotropy leads to qualitatively different effects in these two cases: the ferromagnetic chain is described by a double-sine-Gordon-type equation with phase-shifted harmonics, whereas the antiferromagnetic chain reduces to a sine-Gordon equation. For the latter case, phase boundaries between incommensurate and commensurate states are found analytically in $(H,A,D,δ)$ space and confirmed by numerical calculations for certain $D$ and $δ$ values. Close to all ICTs, results of the continuum consideration become invalid due to a stochastic destruction of near-separatrix solutions which either make an ICT a first-order transition or stabilize states with spatially irregular soliton and antisoliton arrangements.
nd4790050b182: Strongly enhanced superconductivity (SC) (Tc = 73 K) in Ba2CuO3+x (BCO) challenges the longheld paradigm of the irrelevance of the dz2-like states in cuprates. Using tight-binding band structure plus dynamical mean-field theory (TB+DMFT), we find that a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FFL) is the normal state for the parameters realistic for BCO. Transport properties exhibit strange metal behavior above Tcoh~38 K, supporting a direct instability of this strange metal to SC. Irrelevance of one-fermion inter-band mixing, itself a non-trivial consequence of the FFL state, preferentially enhances two-fermion hopping processes and provides a novel route for both SC and competing excitonic order(s) arising directly from the FFL. The proposed scenario also clarifies the role of dz2 band in shaping the physical responses of BCO.
n58c12350d719: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.
ndb92b57593f6: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T<Tc, Delta_lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have any power law dependency with T, which is expected for a nodeless superconducting order parameter. The superfluid density reveals a fully gapped superconductivity with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.02. In the superconducting state, the electronic specific heat is best described by an s-wave BCS model with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.05. All these results from the present study indicate that In2Bi is a typical type-II,BCS-like, strongly coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.
n40a5c975b7b7: Stochastic oscillations are commonly identified through peaks in their power spectra, yet the fundamental limits on their strength and energetic cost remain unclear. Here we establish universal dynamical and thermodynamic bounds on oscillation efficiency in Markov networks, showing how finite state spaces constrain spectral peak enhancement. In particular, we demonstrate that networks maximizing modal coherence need not maximize oscillation efficiency. We further derive dissipation bounds that connect oscillation efficiency to the relaxation speed and stationary probabilities, revealing an unavoidable energetic cost of maintaining pronounced oscillations at a specified relaxation timescale. These bounds remain strictly positive in regimes where existing explicit spectral dissipation estimates vanish, with stronger constraints for normal networks and uniform rings. Our results distinguish spectral oscillatory strength from modal coherence and reveal how network dynamics and thermodynamic dissipation jointly limit stochastic oscillations.
n84eb484e9350: $η$ pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing $η$ pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors $η$-like pairing in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at $X=(π,0)$ and $Y=(0,π)$, which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum $\mathbf Q=(π,π)$, thereby favoring an $η$-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting $η$-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-$4e$-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-$2e$ Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive $η$-like condensate in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets.
n693e88af285e: We demonstrate the emergence of extraordinary-log criticality in a quantum many-body system by coupling a spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg chain to a two-dimensional quantum critical Heisenberg bilayer. Under the quantum-to-classical mapping, the chain acts as a plane defect in a three-dimensional critical environment for which the extraordinary-log universality class has recently been predicted. Using large-scale sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we directly probe the renormalization-group flow of the effective defect coupling through the spin stiffness. We observe the characteristic logarithmic growth with linear system size $L$, corresponding to a stable weak-coupling fixed point and a running coupling $g(L)\sim 1/\log L$. Furthermore, the extracted step-scaling function quantitatively follows the universal renormalization-group flow predicted for the extraordinary-log universality class, including the leading and subleading universal coefficients. Our results establish extraordinary-log criticality in a genuine quantum many-body setting and show that its universal behavior persists despite the topological $θ$-term present in the low-energy field theory of the isolated spin chain.
n829c97c7ea9e: We examine the kinematics of Compton and inverse Compton scattering by Dirac carriers in graphene. Unlike photons in vacuum, which propagate at the speed of light c, graphene carriers have a characteristic velocity vF, with vF much less than c. This difference means that the standard Compton scattering formula cannot be applied to graphene simply by replacing c with vF. We first examine Compton-like scattering for a gapless Dirac carrier initially at the Dirac point and for a gapped carrier at the band edge, both corresponding to zero in-plane momentum. We then consider scattering from an energetic gapless Dirac carrier. By combining energy conservation with the graphene dispersion and in-plane momentum conservation, we obtain a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy within the model considered. This relation is the main kinematic result of the work. We identify inverse Compton-like scattering by the transfer of energy from the carrier to the photon, subject to the simultaneous conservation of energy and in-plane momentum. We also discuss how this process differs kinematically from Doppler-shifted emission, Cerenkov-like radiation, harmonic generation, photon drag, and other nonlinear optical processes. Finally, we propose a time-resolved pump-probe arrangement in which the scattered photon spectrum is the primary observable, while time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) provides an independent probe of the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. These results provide a kinematic framework for analysing inverse Compton-like scattering in graphene and for identifying the conditions under which energy can be transferred from energetic Dirac carriers to photons.
nca1cb33e4869: The square-hexagon-dodecagon (SHD) lattice hosts an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid, while further-neighbor couplings frustrate its Heisenberg magnet into classically degenerate lines where quantum fluctuations can melt the Néel order. To place this state among the lattice's spin liquids, we classify fermionic parton mean-field states with singlet and spin-orbit-coupled triplet amplitudes by their projective symmetry groups (PSGs). As SHD sites lack site symmetry, its $Z_2$ PSGs are the projective classes of $p6mm$ with time reversal, from which those of every single-orbit $p6mm$ lattice follow. In the idealized Kitaev model, where lattice operations do not rotate spins, these liquids carry a single $Z_2$ PSG descending from the $SU(2)$ Lieb-flux state, and their projections are exact eigenstates. The PSG's sixfold-rotation sign, fixed by the dodecagon flux, doubles all Majorana bands, and the mirrors exclude a chiral phase in any uniform field, so only a sublattice-staggered three-spin term drives the non-Abelian Ising phase. Beyond the Kitaev state, we find a critical semi-Dirac spin liquid, with mean-field correlations $\propto r^{-3}$ along three directions and $r^{-6}$ otherwise, and extended Dirac phases with up to $48$ fermion flavors, among them an $N_f=12$ state whose PSG forbids every singlet mass. ne4ee494137b4: Controlling magnon currents is central to the development of magnonic devices, which exploit spin excitations for information transport without charge flow. n49691b93fb90: Understanding how stochastic gradient descent learns internal representations in wide neural networks trained on rich target functions is a central problem in machine learning. We then estimate the timescale of specialization, when Gaussian closure breaks down and individual learned features begin to strongly correlate with specific target features. We finally describe how the activation function determines the pattern of specialization and characterize the subsequent refinement of learned features. n79df042b1e91: We theoretically study dc electric currents induced by rapid spin precession in noncentrosymmetric magnetic Weyl semimetals using the Floquet--Keldysh Green's-function formalism. We further show that a finite Weyl-cone tilt modifies the available interband-transition phase space, smooths the frequency dependence of the current, and allows for a shift current and another type of injection current, both of which flow in directions determined by the tilt and the direction of the precession. A finite net current can remain after summing contributions from Weyl nodes of opposite chiralities when their transition phase spaces are inequivalent.
n4b1e498b0815: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.
n8d6395fb0e2f: The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. Here we construct a six-band multiorbital double helix model parameterized by characteristic B form DNA geometry and hopping scales. The model incorporates major minor groove asymmetry, an axial base pair offset representing stagger, and compositional inequivalence between the two strands, providing structural control parameters with which the orbital response can be tuned. Inter strand hybridization generates a full three component atomic OAM texture in the corotating local helical frame, including a radial component absent in the corresponding single helix model. We separately evaluate the itinerant OAM using the Bloch wave packet formulation of orbital magnetization and identify an additional inter-strand circulation channel unique to the double-helix connectivity. The resulting atomic and itinerant responses have distinct microscopic origins, magnitudes, and temperature dependences, establishing a multiorbital framework for geometry controlled angular momentum generation and transport in chiral molecular conductors.
nc6b2e4bbec5a: We study local $2\times2$ correlations in uniformly random domino tilings of the Aztec diamond $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$, a dimer model with frozen corners and a liquid region bounded by the Arctic circle, and compare them with the square chessboard. The squares form two interleaved sublattices, distinguished by the color of their lower-left cell. On the $L\times L$ chessboard the same rule holds with $n$ replaced by the half-width $L/2$, but the contrast is two to six times weaker, the central edge probability never equals $1/4$, and the maxima of $P_H$ are pinned to the corners. n4dc2719eedf6: We develop a theory for the plastic shear rate $\dotγ_i$ on each slip system $i$ of face-centered cubic (FCC) single crystals, by integrating the shear rate contributions $\dotγ_i(l)$ from dislocation links of length $l$. In particular, it explains why the plastic shear rate depends exponentially on the resolved shear stress $τ_i$, as reported previously, in the absence of any thermally activated mechanism. This dependence arises from the exponential tail of $n_i(l)$ filtered through the threshold-like velocity function $v_i(l)$. Furthermore, $v_i(l)$ is well approximated by a single two-dimensional function $v(τ_i,l)$ for all these slip systems. n575a571c476a: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
nb0af363a5933: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. n12738cad98d4: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.
n8c19db448078: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. nc58e2993c74e: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.
n30904f376ada: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. n682c49175414: Conventional centrifugal sedimentation cannot readily separate particles with the same sedimentation velocities. Both methods separate particles without relying on sedimentation-velocity differences and are expected to preserve particle properties. Because they neither depend on electrical properties nor require a change of medium, they may also be applicable to particles in liquid metals, oils, organic solvents, and ionic liquids.
n97370927a97f: Dense active--passive mixtures are often described within an effective-temperature picture, in which active dopants promote cage breaking and fluidize an arrested amorphous host. ne8bd69d0340d: We analyze the stability and non-linear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) driven by an external magnetic field in the clean limit (i.e., in the absence of disorder and thermal fluctuations). Our theoretical analysis and predicted phase diagram are fully supported by numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the full Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
n1121155e3cbf: The helicity of a magnetic skyrmion in a centrosymmetric frustrated magnet is a soft collective coordinate and a candidate variable for encoding quantum information. Thus, we establish a microscopic connection between helicity dynamics and the excitation spectrum of frustrated skyrmions and identify the symmetry constraints governing dissipation of helicity-based quantum states.
n3495bc8cf76f: Antiferromagnetic insulator α-Fe2O3 is a potential medium for coherent motion of spin waves over relatively large distances, allowing non-dissipative transfer of information between circuit elements. The symmetric voltage coefficient Ks exhibits two approximately linear temperature regimes, separated by a characteristic temperature T* whose value depends on the thickness of the α-Fe2O3 layer. Further, the dc magnetization measurements on some of the samples suggest that the T* is correlated with the spin reorientation transition (Morin transition) in α-Fe2O3. Interestingly, a significantly larger magnitude of dKs/dT is noted below the characteristic temperature T*. The observed thickness and temperature dependent spin-current transmission indicates a sensitivity to the magnetic state of the insulating hematite layer.
n940ae8b0cdd9: Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. We discuss this scenario for CoNb$_4$Se$_8$, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.
na54d909c202d: The one-dimensional chain with alternating masses is the simplest mechanical system with a topological band structure. The evanescent Bloch waves available at each frequency are matched directly to force balance at a free end or a domain wall, without transfer matrices, which yields closed-form frequencies and decay lengths for every localized mode. The free-end mode sits at a branch point of the complex band structure, where the acoustic and optical sheets join and the decay is fastest. For uniform springs, a sharp wall between the two mass orderings hosts one in-gap mode, symmetric at the light$\mid$light wall and antisymmetric at the heavy$\mid$heavy wall, and an adiabatic construction shows that these are the same topological mode; the light$\mid$light wall also binds a non-topological mode above the optical branch. Spectral unfolding makes this classification visible in momentum space: the sign of the Bloch factor sets the zone-center or zone-boundary character of each mode, and its magnitude sets the width. The Zak phase, quantized by inversion, identifies the modes of topological origin and fixes a half-integer mode count per band at a wall, while the chiral symmetry known to be hidden in strain coordinates explains which frequencies are pinned.
n98cdc932f432: Nagaoka polarons are canonical examples of kinetic magnetism. Although their spin structure is well understood, their transport remains unexplored. Upon cooling, an incoherent Drude-like response gives way to a finite-frequency peak as the dc mobility vanishes. The peak signals an internal mode of a hole confined by its ferromagnetic cloud. Our results establish transport as an incisive probe of polaron formation and kinetic self-trapping.
ndcd5fa50c22e: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.
n752b344a3ef5: We demonstrate the existence of type 1.5 like superconductivity in a single component Ginzburg-Landau model with a higher order potential. The solutions take the form of bags that contain vortices of one vacuum inside the other. This gives rise to four different types of vortex interaction, where one set of length scales determines vortex interactions inside the bags and the other set between the bags. Hence, within the bag the vortices can repel or attract and the bags themselves can repel or attract depending on the hierarchy of four length scales. When vortices repel within the bag, solutions act similarly to those in type 1.5 multicomponent superconductors, but in a single component system.
nd61f6cae9016: We investigate phase separation in a binary fluid subjected to a moving Gaussian cooling source and externally imposed material flow. Advection reorganizes the phase-separated domains by transporting, stretching, and reorienting them. At low flow velocities, competing thermal and advective histories produce distinct regions of flow-aligned and vertical layers. A stronger flow aligns the domains predominantly along the flow direction. Our results demonstrate that a moving thermal history can encode a spatial record of non-equilibrium phase separation. This work provides a route to controlled morphology selection through the competition between front propagation, thermal diffusion, and material flow.
na2f6c13f2826: Using the density matrix renormalization group method, we solve the Pariser--Parr--Pople model of $π$-electron systems to determine the character and energies of the low-lying eigenstates of a lycopene dimer comprising two 22-carbon-atom chains. Our results establish a direct connection between carotenoid packing geometry, symmetry-controlled electronic coupling, and the energetically accessible pathways for SF.
nac008a9870be: The HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio has been observed to vary significantly in different astrophysical environments, making it an important diagnostic tool for exploring the interstellar medium. We also find that the isomerization reaction of HOC$^+$ to HCO$^+$ is efficient with both H2 and CO. We were able to assess the impact of our new measured reaction rate coefficients on the predicted HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio using a state-of-the-art astrochemical model.
n7259153aeee9: We have developed a reduced-cost framework for excited-state calculations by combining the state-specific frozen natural orbital (SS-FNO) approach with the third-order algebraic diagrammatic construction [ADC(3)] method and tensor hypercontraction (THC). Benchmark calculations demonstrate that the combined approach achieves excellent agreement with the canonical ADC(3) results. The efficiency of the present implementation is demonstrated by calculating the excitation energy of a molecule containing 31 atoms and more than one thousand basis functions.
n23b65da1a427: The combinatorial explosion in monomial counts limits the extension of global permutationally invariant polynomial (PIP) potential energy surfaces to larger molecular systems. Together, these results show that PIPs are neither inherently restricted to small systems nor intrinsically nontransferable.
n0fb60fe49397: Companion paper I (Khanal and Arunan, in this issue; arXiv:2610.16629 [physics.chem-ph]) reported reference BEs and F-bond distances for two new databases SEFB-15 (DF$\cdots$CH$_3$) and CSFB-14 (DF$\cdots$NH$_3$). Here, we assess performance of popular ab initio methods (MP2, MP3, MP4(DQ), MP4(SDQ), CCSD, and QCISD) with valence- and full-electron correlation treatments, and sixteen Minnesota DFAs, including M06-2X already assessed in companion paper I. CCSD/AVDZ reproduces reference F-bond distances closely, although BEs predicted by it deviate more. Among the 16 Minnesota DFAs, M08-HX reliably reproduces both reference values for DF$\cdots$CH$_3$ and DF$\cdots$NH$_3$, comparable to M05-2X and M06-2X for DF$\cdots$NH$_3$. Selected meta-GGAs (M06-L, M11-L, and MN15-L) exhibit spurious fractional charge transfer in cationic complexes even at infinite separation, whereas hybrid Minnesota DFAs do not, except M05 and M06 for NH$_3$F$^+\cdots$CH$_3$ and NH$_2$F$_2^+\cdots$CH$_3$. Although M08-HX shows slightly larger monomer delocalization error than M05-2X and M06-2X, it is more reliable for predicting BEs of SEFB complexes, indicating that monomer delocalization error alone does not govern DFA performance. Bader's intermolecular delocalization indices (DIs) further support M08-HX as more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for SEFB, while the larger DIs from M05-2X and M06-2X explain the degraded performance of their dispersion-corrected variants for DF$\cdots$CH$_3$, with only a minor impact for DF$\cdots$NH$_3$, highlighting the system-dependent nature of functional delocalization error. Present work reveals that M08-HX is more reliable than M05-2X and M06-2X for open-shell DF$\cdots$CH$_3$ complexes, while all three functionals show comparable reliability for closed-shell DF$\cdots$NH$_3$ complexes.
nc9179878c575: We derive a vibro-polaritonic Raman activity from third-order cavity Born-Oppenheimer perturbation theory (CBO-PT) accounting for weak interactions between electrons and low-frequency cavity modes in the vibrational strong coupling (VSC) regime. This work extends the recently presented CBO-PT linear response approach [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2024, 15, 2262-2269] from infrared (IR) to vibro-polaritonic Raman spectroscopy. In a first step, we discuss cavity-induced corrections to the static dipole polarizability tensor, which manifest as molecular and cavity mode contribution determined by the polarization-projected static hyperpolarizability tensor. We then obtain the corresponding vibro-polaritonic Raman activity in double harmonic approximation, which contains molecular, cavity and mixed contributions similar to previously discussed CBO-PT IR intensities. The cavity Raman activity can be interpreted as effective transmission component, which is exclusively determined by the polaritonic Raman response. The methodology and its relation to vibro-polaritonic IR spectroscopy is illustrated for a formaldehyde molecule under VSC. An implementation of the CBO-PT linear response approach for vibro-polaritonic Raman and IR spectroscopies is provided via the open-source Python package CBOvibSpec.
nd27312b53295: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.
n3d1bdb8badc4: Phase-field models of fracture provide a unified framework for simulating crack nucleation and propagation, but their computational cost remains high because the governing equilibrium and phase-field equations are typically iteratively solved over the entire domain at every staggered iteration. We present an extension of the recently developed adaptive mesh refinement and coarsening framework that localizes not only spatial resolution but also repeated solution effort to a small active patch around the crack tip for linear elastic brittle materials. The inactive exterior is eliminated through a Schur complement and condensed onto the patch interface, and its factorization is reused as long as the patch remains fixed. The phase field is frozen in the exterior, introducing only a small approximation in the crack wake. The method is implemented in FEniCSx and evaluated for quasi-static crack propagation, dynamic crack branching, three-dimensional mixed-mode crack growth, and coalescence of multiple cracks in a unit cell. Across these problems, the condensed formulation reproduces the reference solutions with differences in global quantities below 0.5%, while substantially reducing the number of active degrees of freedom. In the quasi-static surfing problem, wall time speedups increase from 6.9 to 22.8 as the domain size is doubled, demonstrating increasing computational advantage for large-scale phase-field fracture simulations.
n0c1eea75d2c9: Transient microscopy has evolved to include a family of well-established techniques for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of excited states in a variety of materials systems. In these methods, a laser pulse is focused to locally excite a material, and the subsequent evolution of the excited species is visualized to extract transport parameters such as diffusivities. Typically, transport coefficients are extracted from experimental datasets using curve-fitting methods to analyze the change in the mean squared displacement (MSD) of the spatial profiles over time. However, this approach can lead to inaccurate or misleading diffusivity values under many common experimental conditions, and is only formally accurate for the case of a single diffusing species. In this work, we introduce a new approach to the analysis of transient microscopy data based on the evolution of profile shapes in reciprocal space. We use simulated datasets to quantitatively analyze the performance of our proposed methods and compare them to current state-of-the-art analysis techniques. We demonstrate that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods have the highest overall performance in terms of accuracy and precision for normal diffusive transport over a range of realistic initial conditions and signal-to-noise ratios. Furthermore, we highlight the limitations of using MSD alone to characterize anomalous transport in materials, and we show how analysis of spatial frequencies can yield a more comprehensive understanding of complex excited-state dynamics and their underlying physical mechanisms. Our results show that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods are powerful tools for characterizing and quantifying many different types of transport behaviors.
n11e5389846fa: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. We then show that increasing the photoexcited carrier density enhances both the initial total force and the plasma-shifted equilibrium position of the $A_{1g}$ mode, producing larger coherent lattice oscillations. This density-controlled response appears in both the atomic displacement and the coherent-phonon-induced band renormalization, providing complementary signatures for ultrafast reflectivity and time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
nac5a3b64806a: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constraints, leading to different accessible site densities and blocking capabilities. Beyond coverage, we highlight the importance of the reactivity of adsorbed inhibitor fragments toward precursors in determining inhibitor stability and blocking performance. Together, these findings demonstrate the need to consider both steric effects and chemical reactivity on realistic amorphous surfaces. Our calculations connect local reaction chemistry with inhibitor coverage and provide a computational basis for understanding inhibition mechanisms and selecting suitable inhibitor-precursor combinations for AS-ALD.
nf834b0295fad: The length-gauge (LG) time-dependent Liouville equation is a major workhorse to simulate ultrafast dynamics. The equation features the commutator between the density operator $\hatρ$ and the position operator ${\bf r}$, $\langle n{\bf k}|[{\bf r},\hatρ]|m{\bf k}'\rangle$, where $|n{\bf k}\rangle$ and $|m{\bf k}'\rangle$ are Bloch states for bands $n$ and $m$ at crystal momenta ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, respectively. This commutator has two irreconcilable versions: Kohn and Luttinger (Phys. Rev. ${\bf 108}$, 590 (1954)) have two partial derivatives with respect to ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, but Aversa and Sipe (AS) (Phys. Rev. B ${\bf 52}$, 14636 (1995)) have one partial derivative and one Dirac delta. For several decades, this outstanding discrepancy has received little attention. Here, we show that the generalized LG time-dependent Liouville equation has two partial derivatives, but no Dirac delta. Physically, the ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements of the position operator provide a channel by which the electric field generates ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements for $\hatρ$ in LG. The discrepancy emerges when the position matrix is assumed to be diagonal in ${\bf k}$. Consequently the AS' equation is a limiting case of our generalized Liouville equation, where the relative momentum ${\bf Q}$ between two states is ignored. Our numerical test reveals that the ${\bf k}$-diagonal formalism yields qualitatively different results and underestimates both energy absorption and polarization by a factor of 7. Our study establishes a general formalism for the length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation and opens the door for future research on the ultrafast time scale, while prior results based on the ${\bf k}$-diagonal only equation may need to be revisited.
nd377380d166c: During fuel-cladding chemical interaction (FCCI), lanthanide fission products generated in the fuel can migrate into cladding grain boundaries (GBs), where segregation may reduce GB strength and promote corrosion cracking. For each material, segregation energies, work-of-separation values for complete interfacial cleavage, and traction-separation curves measuring ideal resistance to crack opening were evaluated within a consistent computational framework. Nd and Ce segregate favorably to both materials, and the median segregation energies are more negative in TiN, showing that TiN does not simply exclude these species from internal interfaces. The mechanical responses of Fe and TiN differ sharply. In Fe, Nd and Ce consistently reduce work of separation and peak traction, with median work-of-separation retentions of 0.72 and 0.65 and median peak-traction retentions of 0.47 and 0.43. In TiN, most decorated GBs preserve much of the clean response, with median work-of-separation retentions of 1.00 and 0.97 and median peak-traction retention of 0.85 for both fission products. Bonding analysis shows weak, occupied antibonding X-Fe replacement bonds in Fe, whereas the surrounding Ti-N network remains largely preserved after Nd/Ce segregation in TiN. These results provide atomistic support for the use of TiN and related nitride coatings to reduce FCCI damage by retaining GB strength if fission products segregate to coating internal interfaces. This retention of GB strength also provides a mechanistic descriptor for assessing coating susceptibility to FCCI-assisted corrosion cracking and environmentally assisted intergranular fracture.
n74b09415f626: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. Monte Carlo simulations comparing H, He, C, and O implantation predicted a narrower vacancy-distribution profile for hydrogen under the implantation conditions examined. Raman spectroscopy was used to evaluate implantation-induced lattice damage and its recovery during annealing and membrane release, while optical bandgap analysis provided further evidence of restoration of the diamond lattice structure. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. The SCDms were subsequently transferred to GaN, SiC, AlGaN, and AlN substrates without an adhesive layer. The successful formation of diamond/WBG and diamond/UWBG heterostructures demonstrates the feasibility of integrating the SCDms with a range of semiconductor platforms. Overall, these results establish hydrogen implantation as an effective route for producing high-quality SCDms for future diamond-based heterogeneous integration applications.
n9e8f309906d4: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.
nda779c43e766: Supermagnetic states are typically set during synthesis. Changing and retaining these states requires sustained external stimulus. Without resynthesis or continued stimulus, we show, for the first time, a reversible magneto-ionic switching between superferromagnetic (SFM) and superspin-glass (SSG) states using room-temperature Li-ion transport. We utilize the incomplete lithiation of NiO into nanoscale Ni and Li2O to switch between the states. Lithiation generates a fragmented nano-Ni network that strengthens dipolar interactions and promotes SFM order with stronger memory and higher room-temperature moments. Delithiation partially regenerates NiO and drives the system into an SSG state with higher low-temperature coercivity and sharper temperature-selective memory. The interconversion between SFM and SSG persists at all measured subsequent lithiation-delithiation cycles, creating a general framework for supermagnetic switching.
n21f92a5bef58: The electronic self-energy determines the single-particle Green's function and, through it, quasiparticle energies and spectral functions, but computing it from first principles is expensive and it is a difficult machine-learning target: complex-valued, matrix-valued in a local-orbital basis, and dependent on a continuous frequency. We predict the dynamical correlation part of the imaginary-frequency G_0W_0 self-energy matrix of molecules from atomic species and coordinates with an E(3)-equivariant message-passing network, the rotational covariance of the orbital-space matrix being imposed by the architecture itself and the static exchange part taken from the density-functional reference. Frequency enters either as an explicit network input or through frequency-specific output heads, and the predicted matrices are continued to the real axis in a representation in which causality and a non-negative spectral density hold by construction. The frequency-conditioned model reproduces matrix elements to below 1 meV on the imaginary axis for the systems studied here, and that accuracy survives the continuation: for water clusters, including a tetramer absent from the training set, and for chemically diverse molecules from QM9, the reconstructed spectral functions follow the G_0W_0 reference peak by peak and the frontier quasiparticle levels are recovered to a few tens of meV. Learning the self-energy on the imaginary axis is therefore a practical route to real-frequency spectra: once the model is trained, and given the density-functional reference it is built on, a new geometry costs no explicit G_0W_0 calculation.
n9b4f47e3ec0d: Control of magnetic anisotropy is essential for the fabrication of next-generation devices in spintronics and magnetic memory. While conventional approaches such as material composition, thermal annealing, and ion bombardment are widely used, achieving spatially resolved, continuous control remains a challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a dual-regime, localized control over both transient magnetic states and permanent intrinsic properties in perpendicularly magnetized Co/Pt multilayers using ultra-short laser pulses. By employing a multi-scale approach combining Kerr microscopy, magnetic force microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, we reveal that low-fluence irradiation enables a reversible, helicity-dependent accumulation of magnetic phases without altering the intrinsic quasistatic properties. Conversely, high-fluence exposure acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently hardens the magnetic system. This structural relaxation leads to a substantial enhancement of the effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving a twofold increase in the local coercive field and expanding the equilibrium stripe domain width. By offering both reversible spin manipulation and deterministic engineering of 2D magnetic landscapes, this work paves the way towards flexible, lithography-free anisotropy structuring for advanced spintronic applications.
n977ccb173617: Phonon calculations with machine-learned interatomic potentials are almost exclusively performed with finite displacements in supercells, an approach that is exact only at wave vectors commensurate with the supercell and whose error depends on the range of the force constants. In message-passing networks this range grows with the number of layers, and reaches 140 angstrom for the deepest universal models. Here we show that the dynamical matrix of a message-passing potential can be obtained exactly in the primitive cell, at any wave vector, as the linear response of the forces to a displacement modulated by a Bloch phase, in the spirit of density-functional perturbation theory. The phase enters only where the features of neighboring atoms are gathered, and the trained model is used without modification. One further derivative yields group velocities and mode Grüneisen parameters analytically. We apply the method to NequIP and Prophet, and reproduce the Hessians of supercells to machine precision. Using these results as a reference, we find that the supercells commonly employed in high-throughput calculations lead to errors of several tenths of a THz in the phonon frequencies, and that these errors decrease slowly with the size of the supercell, in particular for deep models. For a low-symmetry silicate, the supercell predicts a dynamical instability that the model does not have. Quantities that depend on derivatives of the dispersion, such as the group velocities and the Grüneisen parameter at low temperature, are considerably more affected than the frequencies themselves. When both approaches are used to obtain the same force constants, their computational cost is comparable for crystals with symmetry.
n6323cae7b4b5: Magnetic fields drive grain boundary migration in non-magnetic systems through anisotropic susceptibility, yet how the local orientation can affect the resulting collective grain growth behavior remains unclear. We employ a phase-field model to investigate magnetic-field-assisted grain growth in the diamagnetic Bi. This study provides a mechanistic basis for using static and dynamically varied magnetic fields to control texture development and grain growth kinetics in weakly magnetic materials. We also identify the conditions under which magnetic-field-driven orientation selection produces a distinct bimodal grain-size distribution. The bicrystal studies establish that boundary migration is governed by the magnetic free-energy difference between differently oriented grains, while polycrystalline field-sweep simulations reveal a transition from capillary-dominated coarsening to magnetically biased texture selection. For unbiased orientation distributions, magnetic selection remains distributed; however, when a small population of grains is strongly favored, the driving force localizes and exhibits bimodal coarsening characterized by enlarged favored grains embedded within a fine-grained matrix, even without grain boundary energy anisotropy, particle pinning, or heterogeneity. The field removal and field reorientation simulations further show that magnetic field history can redirect the coarsening pathway.
n23f29270802b: The realization of artificial magnetic structures with high epitaxial quality and elevated critical temperatures remains a key challenge for spintronics. Here, we report the fabrication and characterization of epitaxial (La2/3Sr1/3MnO3)3/(BaTiO3)3 trilayer heterostructures grown by layer-by-layer laser ablation. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, magnetization measurements, and neutron diffraction confirm their exceptional crystalline order and the absence of structural defects. Neutron diffraction reveals no antiferromagnetic Bragg peaks, ruling out most antiferromagnetic configurations with a non zero wave vector Q. Magnetic hysteresis loops instead evidence a ferromagnetic order with a remanent moment of about 0.5 bohr magneton per Mn atom at room temperature, persisting either in-plane or out-of-plane depending on the applied field. Our findings highlight neutron diffraction as a powerful tool for elucidating the magnetic structure of complex thin films and suggest that weak interlayer coupling through BaTiO3 leads to ferromagnetism with a high critical temperature (about 600 K).
nffefcb02465e: We have reanalyzed the 0.25 and 0.50 monolayer (ML) phases of oxygen on the catalytically important Rh(100) surface by quantitative low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), variable-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and density functional theory (DFT). For the (2$\times$2)-O phase at 0.25 ML we find oxygen adsorbed at fourfold hollow sites in accordance to earlier results [Surf. Sci. 207 (1988) 55], however, with a pronounced buckling within the second layer of the otherwise unreconstructed substrate. For the 0.50 monolayer phase, we recently identified a (2$\sqrt{2}$ $\times$ 2$\sqrt{2}$)R45$^\circ$-4O ground state structure [Phys. Rev. Res. 8 (2026) 023296], which decomposes into a large number of nano-domains already at temperatures below 100 K. In this paper we provide a detailed analysis of the atomic structure and the ordering behavior of this phase and resolve long-standing discrepancies with the original (2$\times$2)pg model [Phys. Rev. Lett. 82 (1999) 4874]. We further prove by short-range order simulations that the coherent superposition of scattering contributions of the nano-domains leads to a virtual extinction of diffraction spots, which has concealed the true periodicity and symmetry of this phase for so long.
n2362f2743131: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the \texttt{nvalchemi} platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \ce{Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O3}, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of $6.8 \pm 0.7$~mS/cm in amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.
n51ff07e1d599: We perform molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of AlTi metallic alloy melts, with a specific focus on surface properties and the effect of oxygen. The simulations use a machine-learned inter- action potential (MLIP) that has recently been tested through experimental data for the statical and dynamical properties of AlTi melts in the bulk [Kato et al. (2026)]. We find that the surface- tension response to oxygen depends strongly on the AlTi composition. Element-resolved density profiles show that oxygen enrichment near the interface is accompanied by a suppression of the Al surface segregation observed in the oxygen-free liquid. The results are compared to experimental values obtained using levitation techniques in microgravity.
ne4a6ded855e5: We present a retrospective on the Python Materials Genomics (pymatgen) library, reflecting on 15 years of community growth and established best practices. The current version of pymatgen builds on its robust, open-source foundation, emphasising its collaborative nature. Over the past decade, pymatgen has thrived as one of the largest open-source materials science codebases. We detail how pymatgen supports advanced computational materials science workflows, how it adapts to changing demands, and the lessons learned from its growing community, providing guidance beyond pymatgen's open-source community. Pymatgen will continue to evolve in response to the current rapidly changing landscape of computational materials science and materials informatics. We discuss the challenges and potential solutions to managing the community-driven evolution of pymatgen and provide an outlook on its future development.
n45502fcccf1b: This paper describes topas-editor and TOPilot, which provide a powerful interface to the TOPAS software suite and allow generative AI-driven automation of complex crystallographic tasks. topas-editor is a TOPAS-aware VS Code extension designed for the rapid creation and editing of TOPAS input files and for interacting with the software. It knows TOPAS syntax, has crystallographic-aware editing features and provides in-line user guidance via hover tips and automated links to reference manuals. TOPilot is a collection of Python routines and machine-accessible reference documents that allow AI-driven automated analysis in TOPAS. It uses a transferable topas-inp-writer skill that can be applied in all TOPAS application areas. We demonstrate the power and reliability of the approach using examples including: a complex Rietveld refinement with sample- and data-related complications; automatic analysis of multiple data sets; a pipeline from indexing through structure solution to refinement; automatic identification of the phases present in a sample; single crystal and powder diffraction analysis of incommensurate structures; and fitting PDF data. TOPilot can be used directly alongside topas-editor, via a stand-alone topilot-wizard, or via command line interfaces or desktop apps from major AI providers. TOPilot was developed and tested using Claude large language models, but can be configured to use other cloud or local models. topas-editor and TOPilot are freely available.
n6982db230dbb: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.
n6041412a90cd: Single-shot coherent Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering (CRBS) requires dual colour, frequency, and pulse duration agile laser systems, currently available only in laboratory layouts. In this work, we present a compact, portable, and robust next generation laser system that meets all of these requirements. Key features include an integrated master-slave seed laser design for stable frequency chirping, fiber-coupled acousto-optic modulator (AOM) gated pulse shaping for long-term thermal stability, and customized amplification stages in a rugged, portable enclosure which simplifiy the alignment and maintenance process. The system in this implementation can deliver up to $450$~mJ per arm, chirp rates up to $\sim22$~MHz$/$ns, and arbitrary temporal profiles within $\sim25$~ns to $\sim1$~$μ$s. This laser system is validated by measuring the neutral number density of an atmospheric plasma jet, and a two-dimensional temperature map is constructed, demonstrating lab-grade diagnostics for field deployment.
n8d31250b724b: We open the quantum baker map with a position window of width $w$ and center $q_c$.
